root_cause.text: The vulnerability stems from incorrect `ARRAY_SIZE` macros in the Tegra CBB fabric lookup tables that calculated the size of a different target map array than the one referenced, causing out-of-bounds access during timeout lookups.
root_cause.evidence: The patch corrects `drivers/soc/tegra/cbb/tegra234-cbb.c` by changing `ARRAY_SIZE(tegra234_bpmp_target_map)` to `ARRAY_SIZE(tegra234_aon_target_map)` for the AON fabric entry and `ARRAY_SIZE(tegra241_cbb_target_map)` to `ARRAY_SIZE(tegra241_bpmp_target_map)` for the BPMP fabric entry, ensuring the size matches the actual target map pointer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Corrected a copy-paste error where the CBB target map size was incorrectly used for the BPMP fabric target map initialization.
intent_record.what: Replaced ARRAY_SIZE(tegra241_cbb_target_map) with ARRAY_SIZE(tegra241_bpmp_target_map) in the T234_BPMP_FABRIC_ID entry of the tegra241_cbb_fab_list array.
intent_record.how: Ensures the correct size of the BPMP target map is provided during initialization, preventing potential out-of-bounds access or incorrect iteration counts when the CBB and BPMP map sizes differ.
